newsitem.title: DUBAI: Gulf middle distillates hurt by India.
newsitem.headline: Gulf middle distillates hurt by India.

text.p: Gulf diesel premiums to Middle East price quotes faltered on Monday after India Oil Corp (IOC) decided to buy just 165,000 tonnes in its August spot tender and to cancel its middle distillate term tender, traders said.
One percent Gulf gas oil was talked at parity to plus 10 cents over the quote on Monday, down from 10-20 cents ahead of the IOC tenders, with 0.5 percent material down to +20 cents.
"The Indian result was very disappointing for sellers. It has depressed the market and there's no other real requirements," said one Gulf-based trader.
The market had expected IOC to take some 400,000 tonnes in its August tender compared to 855,000 tonnes in July, but the state firm awarded just four spot cargoes to Shell and Mobil.
IOC's tender for term supplies for August 1997-March 1998 delivery was cancelled outright. IOC is expected to enter term supply talks with state Gulf refiners next month.
Scant Indian buying left the Gulf market weighed down with middle distillate material from Saudi Arabia and Kuwait, pushing kerosene down to near parity to price quotes, traders said.
Some traders also said that Iran had offered spot gas oil cargoes though this could not be confirmed.
"It's a buyer's market," said one trader.
Gas oil was talked around $20.05 a barrel fob Gulf, adrift from the year-high of $31.50.
